evidence.interaction: Keyboard at 1440: Tab runs logo > 4 nav links > header CTA > hero CTA > load > rig > crane > radius > ground > mat, with a 3px solid outline at every stop and no traps. Edge inputs at 390: emptying Load, typing '-5' or typing 'abc' is silently treated as 0 t, and the sheet shows a green 'Within 75% of chart, 10%' verdict. Rigging '-3' is likewise dropped to 0. No error or invalid state is shown, even though validity.valid=false for -5. Values above max=200 are accepted ('99999' gives 1010101%). A 20-digit load overflows the page to scrollWidth 464 at 390. Inserting '12,5' into Load gave 125 t. There is no reset control. Changing the crane correctly clamps the radius (100 t at 44 m, then 25 t at 22 m), and 'Made ground' shows the 'Ground not established' stop. No console errors.
evidence.copy: Site vocabulary is used precisely: 'hook block never gets deducted', 'by torchlight', 'not onto a Post-it', 'Change on the day... re-signed 09:15'. Verdict microcopy states the figure and the remedy: 'Shorter radius, bigger crane or more counterweight.' Button labels say exactly what happens.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: a specific promise, the operable sample check (verdict 'Exceeds chart at 14.0 m') and the CTA are all in view. 390: the H1, lede and CTA are in view, but only the 'Lift check' header strip of the artifact shows. Nothing that backs the promise is visible on the phone's first screen.

problems: The lift check silently coerces empty, negative and non-numeric load or rigging to 0 and then shows a green 'Within 75% of chart' verdict. Out-of-range values are accepted, a 20-digit value overflows the page at 390, and there is no reset or error state. This is the wrong failure mode for a safety-check demo.

Phone ergonomics: the header CTA is 37px tall, the inputs 40px and the range 16px. Section nav is removed below 760px with no menu. SVG annotation text shrinks to about 7px, and the artifact starts below the first screen.
The hard-coded fallback figures in the markup (11.2 t / 113%) disagree with the script's own output (10.8 t / 109%), and the signed-record example has no visible 'example' label.

evidence.clarity: H1 'Lift plans that read the load chart for you', then 'Liftplan is a lift plan app for construction sites. Enter the load, the crane, the radius and the ground...' and 'Request a site pilot'. At both 1440 and 390, a stranger can repeat what it is and what to do next.
evidence.fit: A dedicated section reads 'The appointed person signs. Liftplan never does.', with a 'Filled by Liftplan' / 'Decided by the appointed person' split, and the sample sheet's AP boxes say 'Decided by the appointed person'. However, the demo stamps lifts above 90% as 'Not issued' and says 'A pass on the chart with a fail on the ground is still not issued', so the tool acts as a gate. The thresholds are labelled as samples. All CTAs go to https://liftplan.example/pilot.
evidence.distinctiveness: Hazard-tape header rule, condensed uppercase display type, a monospace data face and a numbered lift-plan sheet with a highlighted chart-row strip. Below the hero the structure is a conventional sequence of h2 sections, and the page leans on the form layout rather than a site image.
evidence.proof: The operable sample begins at y=462 at 1440 and y=515 at 390, and the % of chart readout is visible in the first viewport at 390. Changing any control updates both the readout and the six-part sheet, and the chart strip marks the row used (aria-current). The numbers are internally consistent: gross 12.9 = 12.0 + 0.9, 12.9/19.0 = 68%, pad load 0.75 × (60 + 12.9) = 54.7 t.
evidence.craft: Spacing tokens --s1..--s6 and colour tokens are used throughout, with a reset, :where() overflow-wrap and a skip link. axe found no violations, the smallest text is 13px, and there is no overflow at any width. Minor issues: a duplicated '.btn-hi:hover' rule. With JS off, the mobile nav renders permanently open over the hero, because .nav:not([hidden]) shows it and only the script sets hidden. 35 KB HTML, no web fonts loaded (Inter is only a local() preference), and og/twitter images point to the brief's domain.
evidence.mobile: At 390, every link, button, select and range is at least 44px tall. The Menu button works: tap opens it, Escape closes it and returns focus to Menu, tabbing past the last item closes it, tapping a link closes it and lands the section below the sticky header (h-checks top=112), and an outside tap closes it. The CTA is full width, and the sheet's key-value rows turn into right-aligned lines. The sticky readout (134px) plus the header (72px) take about 24% of the screen while you are in the controls.
evidence.honesty: 'Sample lift and chart, written for this page. Not a manufacturer's chart.' sits directly under the artifact title at 390. The pad-load rule is marked 'a sample rule for this page' and the thresholds 'Sample thresholds'. The footer repeats that the sample is illustrative. The pilot section says 'They have asked not to be named yet, so there are no logos here.' No numbers beyond the brief.
evidence.interaction: Operated every state at 1440. Load End reached 268% 'Not issued' with a remedy line. Load Home gave 10% 'Within chart'. Radius 34 m on the 30 m boom gave 'chart ends at 24 m... no rated capacity'. The 40 m boom at 4 m gave 'no chart row under 6 m'. Soft ground at 24 m gave 'Ground fails... mats of at least 5.0 m² needed'. 15.5 t at 11 m gave the 86% amber 'above 75 %' flag. 'Reset to the sample lift' restores the 68% defaults and keeps focus on the button. Inputs are constrained to ranges and selects, so there is no invalid typed state, and the script also guards out-of-range values. The status is announced via role=status. No console errors. Defect: the sticky readout hides focused controls when you Shift+Tab back up. At 390 the radius slider (bottom 189) ends up under the readout (bottom 198). At 720x450, which equals 200% zoom at 1440, the boom select and the load slider are fully hidden under it (WCAG 2.4.11).
evidence.copy: Specific and consistent: 'Rounded up to the next chart row, never interpolated.', 'net + rigging = gross', 'radius 11 m → row 12 m', 'Go or no-go on the day: Wind, ground after rain, visibility'. The reset label says exactly what it does. The page is shorter than A, with less on what the tool replaces.
evidence.first_screen: 1440: the H1, subhead, CTA with 'A pilot runs on one site. Your appointed person still signs every lift.' and the top of the sample (68% 'Within chart' readout plus the Lift plan sheet header) are in view. 390: the H1, subhead, full-width CTA, the sample label and the 68% readout are all in the first viewport.

problems: On phones and at 200% zoom, the sticky .readout fully covers focused controls when tabbing backwards (390: radius slider; 720x450: boom select and load slider). This fails focus-not-obscured.

The demo's 'Not issued' stamp above a 90% sample threshold, or on a ground failure, presents Liftplan as gating the lift. That sits uneasily with the brief's rule not to suggest it replaces the appointed person's judgment, even though it is labelled as a sample rule.
Without JS, the mobile nav renders permanently open over the hero and the Menu button is inert. There is also a duplicated '.btn-hi:hover' rule.

reason: B is the page I would rather maintain. Its artifact is constrained so it cannot reach a misleading state, every edge state has specific feedback, there is a reset, all phone targets are at least 44px, the mobile menu behaves correctly and the CSS uses tokens. A's lift check shows a green 'within chart' verdict for empty or negative loads and has no reset or validation. I would change my mind if A added input validation and reset and B's sticky readout were judged a worse defect than A's coercion bug.
